Pre-wrath teaches that the church will face Antichrist's persecution in the second half of the seventieth week. The rapture comes after the cosmic signs of the sixth seal, and the Day of the Lord's wrath follows at once (Matthew 24:29-31).
Amillennialists do not believe in a literal second coming or a real new earth.
Amillennialism is about how to read Revelation 20, not about whether Christ returns. Amillennialists confess a bodily, visible return as the historic creeds do.
Amillennialists teach one visible return of Christ, one general resurrection and judgment, and a renewed physical creation. Writers such as Anthony Hoekema stress the new earth strongly.
Amillennialists say 'a thousand' means nothing.
Amillennialists do give the number meaning. They read it as a symbol, as numbers often are in Revelation.

Amillennialists read the thousand years as a complete and perfect period: ten cubed. It stands for the whole time between Christ's first and second comings, when Satan is restrained and the saints reign with Christ.
Postmillennialists think the world gets better by human effort, like the social gospel.

Classic postmillennialists such as Jonathan Edwards, Charles Hodge and B. B. Warfield taught that only the Holy Spirit, working through the gospel, brings the growth of the kingdom. The liberal social gospel is a different movement.

Postmillennialists hold that Christ now reigns, and that through preaching and the Spirit most of the world will be converted before he returns. They see this as God's work and a fulfilment of promises such as Psalms 2:8.
Postmillennialists deny that there will be a great apostasy.
Many postmillennialists do expect a final rebellion. Revelation 20:7-9 describes one at the end of the thousand years.

Postmillennialists differ on details. Some place the apostasy of 2 Thessalonians 2:3 in the first century. Others expect a brief falling away just before the return, after a long period of gospel success.
Premillennialists are pessimists who do not care about the world.
Premillennialists have founded missions, hospitals, schools and relief work. They expect Christ to bring the kingdom, but not that Christians should stop doing good.

Premillennialists expect evil to remain strong until the return, and Christ to reign on earth afterwards. Many see this hope as a reason for urgent evangelism and faithful service now (1 Corinthians 15:58).
Stewarding the kingdom now
'Occupy till I come' means Christians should seize political power.
In Luke 19:13 the servants are told to trade with their master's money until he returns. The point is faithful work with what is entrusted, not taking control.
Those who stress stewardship read the parable as a call to faithful use of gifts, time and influence in every area of life. Few of them argue for force or for the church ruling the state.
Stewardship views think the church builds the kingdom without Christ.
No major stewardship or transformational view says the church builds the kingdom apart from Christ. They speak of Christ already reigning and working through his people by the Spirit.
These views hold that the kingdom was inaugurated at Christ's first coming (Matthew 28:18). The church serves as a sign and agent of that rule now, and Christ alone completes it at his return.
Kingdom established at the return
Those who expect the kingdom at the return think nothing done now matters.
Those who expect the kingdom at the return still teach that believers' works will be judged and rewarded (2 Corinthians 5:10). They urge evangelism, good works and holy living.

These views hold that Christ himself will establish his kingdom in power at his coming, not the church. Present work matters as faithful witness and as service that will be rewarded, even though it does not bring the kingdom.
Is there a future seven-year tribulation, Daniel's seventieth week?
Many read Daniel 9:27 as a future seven-year period still to come. Others see it fulfilled in Christ's first coming and AD 70, or as a picture of the whole church age.
Yes, a future seven-year period
A future time of distress, but not a fixed seven years
No, it is fulfilled or spans the church age
Is the church distinct from Israel in God's plan, so that the seventieth week concerns Israel?
Dispensationalists keep Israel and the church distinct, and see the seventieth week as Israel's time. Others see one people of God, while many still expect a future for ethnic Israel.
Yes, they are distinct
One people of God, though Israel has a future
Could Christ come for the church at any moment, before any sign?
Pretribulationists stress imminence: texts tell believers to watch and wait. Others say Paul lists events that must come first (2 Thessalonians 2:3).
Yes, at any moment
No, some signs come first
Is the 'tribulation' the same as God's wrath? When does God's wrath fall?
Believers are not appointed to wrath (1 Thessalonians 5:9). The views differ on whether the whole seven years is wrath, or only part of it.
The whole seven years is God's wrath
Wrath begins at the midpoint
Wrath begins after the cosmic signs, late in the second half
Wrath falls at the end, at Christ's return
Does Matthew 24:31 describe the rapture?
Jesus says the angels will gather the elect after the tribulation. Posttribulationists see the rapture here. Pretribulationists often see the regathering of Israel.
Yes, all believers are gathered once, at the visible return
Partly: watchful believers may be taken earlier
No, it is Israel's regathering; the church is removed earlier
Does Revelation 20 follow the second coming in time?

Premillennialists read Revelation 19 and 20 in sequence: Christ returns, then reigns a thousand years. Amillennialists and postmillennialists see Revelation 20 as going back to describe the church age.
Yes, Christ reigns on earth after his return
No, it describes the present age
Will the gospel win most of the world before the return?

Postmillennialists point to promises that the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord (Habakkuk 2:14). Amillennialists expect the kingdom to grow, but good and evil to grow together until the harvest (Matthew 13:30).
Yes, most nations will be converted
No, wheat and weeds grow together until the end
Is the church's task mainly rescue and witness, or also renewal of culture?
Two-kingdoms writers keep the church to word, sacrament and witness, while Christians serve faithfully as citizens. Kuyperian writers stress Christ's claim over every sphere of life.
Mainly witness; Christians serve in civic life as citizens
Also renewal of every sphere as a sign of the kingdom
Pretribulational dispensational premillennialism

You expect Christ to take the church before a future seven-year tribulation, which concerns Israel and brings God's wrath. After it Christ returns to reign on earth for a thousand years. This is the view of Walvoord, Pentecost and Ryrie, and, in a modified form, of many progressive dispensationalists.
Midtribulational premillennialism

You expect the rapture at the midpoint of the seventieth week, often linked to the last trumpet. The church faces the first half but not the wrath of the second. Gleason Archer defended a form of this view, and Christ then reigns for a thousand years.
Pre-wrath premillennialism

You expect the church to face Antichrist's persecution, and to be raptured after the cosmic signs but before the Day of the Lord's wrath. Christ later reigns on earth for a thousand years. Marvin Rosenthal and Robert Van Kampen developed this view, and Alan Kurschner defends it today.
Historic posttribulational premillennialism

You expect believers to be gathered once, at Christ's visible return after the tribulation, followed by a reign on earth. This view, held by George Ladd and Robert Gundry, claims roots in early writers such as Irenaeus and Justin Martyr.
Partial-rapture premillennialism

You expect watchful, faithful believers to be taken before the tribulation, and others later. Writers such as Robert Govett and G. H. Lang held this view. Critics answer that Scripture links the rapture to being in Christ, not to degree of faithfulness.

You expect the gospel, by the Spirit, to win most of the world before Christ returns once to raise the dead and judge. Jonathan Edwards, Charles Hodge, B. B. Warfield and Loraine Boettner held this view, and Keith Mathison defends it today.
Amillennialism (one coming), two-kingdoms

You see the millennium as the present reign of Christ and the saints, ending with one visible return. The church's mission is word, sacrament and witness, while believers serve faithfully as citizens in the common kingdom. Michael Horton and David VanDrunen represent this emphasis.
Amillennialism (one coming), Kuyperian

You see the millennium as the present reign of Christ, ending with one visible return and a renewed creation. You stress Christ's claim over every sphere of life, so cultural work is a sign of the coming kingdom. Abraham Kuyper and Anthony Hoekema represent this emphasis.
Who wrote 'The Blessed Hope' (1956), a defence of posttribulationism?
Robert Gundry
Dwight Pentecost
George Ladd wrote it. He argued that the 'blessed hope' of Titus 2:13 is Christ's visible return, not a secret earlier rapture.
In which period did John Nelson Darby begin teaching a pretribulational rapture?
Darby developed and taught the view from the late 1820s to the early 1830s, including at the Powerscourt conferences in Ireland.
Which book did Marvin Rosenthal publish in 1990?
The Rapture Question
Rosenthal's book launched the pre-wrath view widely. 'The Rapture Question' is Walvoord's, 'Things to Come' is Pentecost's, and 'The Church and the Tribulation' is Gundry's.
The Niagara Bible Conference, a key premillennial gathering in North America, later divided over what?
Infant baptism
The date of Revelation
Speaking in tongues
Niagara leaders agreed on premillennialism, but in the 1890s some, such as Robert Cameron, moved to posttribulationism, while others held pretribulationism.
Which verse do many take as the origin of the word 'rapture', from the Latin rapiemur, 'we shall be caught up'?
The Latin Vulgate translates the Greek harpazo in 1 Thessalonians 4:17 with a form of rapere, which gives the English word.
Revelation 3:10 promises to keep the faithful 'from the hour of trial'. How do posttribulationists usually read it?
As removal from the earth before it
As protection through the trial
As fulfilled only in AD 70
As a promise only to Israel
Posttribulationists compare John 17:15, where Jesus asks God to keep his people from evil, not to take them out of the world. Pretribulationists read it as removal from the time itself.
How many times does the phrase 'thousand years' occur in Revelation 20?
Once
Three times
Six times
Ten times
It occurs six times in Revelation 20:2-7. All views agree on the count; they differ on its meaning and timing.
Which early church writer admitted that some orthodox Christians did not hold his premillennial view?
Augustine
Origen
Eusebius
In his Dialogue with Trypho, Justin Martyr affirmed a reign in a rebuilt Jerusalem, but said many true Christians thought otherwise.
Whose work 'The City of God' shaped the amillennial reading of Revelation 20 for centuries?
Irenaeus
Thomas Aquinas
Augustine read the thousand years as the present age of the church, with Satan bound so that he cannot stop the gospel's spread.
Which theologian is closely linked to the claim that Christ says 'Mine!' over every square inch of life?
Abraham Kuyper
Charles Spurgeon
Abraham Kuyper said this at the opening of the Free University of Amsterdam in 1880. It is a key idea for transformational, Kuyperian views of culture.
Which of these is a classic postmillennial writer?
J. N. Darby
Jonathan Edwards expected a great age of gospel success before Christ's return. Darby, Ryrie and Lindsey were pretribulational premillennialists.
In the parable of Luke 19:11-27, what does the nobleman tell his servants to do until he returns?
Seize the city
Build him a palace
Trade with the money he gave them
Wait on the mountain
The KJV renders it 'Occupy till I come'. The servants are to work with what he entrusted to them, and are judged on their faithfulness when he returns.
What did the Scofield Reference Bible (1909) do for dispensational premillennialism?
It rejected the rapture
It spread the view widely through its notes
It introduced postmillennialism
It was the first Bible in Tamil
Scofield's notes carried dispensational and pretribulational teaching to a very wide English-speaking readership.
Which text do postmillennialists often cite for Christ reigning until all his enemies are defeated?
Psalms 110:1 says the Lord's anointed sits at God's right hand until his enemies are made his footstool. 1 Corinthians 15:25 applies this to Christ's present reign.
Christ will return bodily and visibly
Every view holds that the same Jesus who ascended will come back in person and in glory. His return is the hope of the church and the goal of history.
The dead will rise and the living will be changed

All views affirm that believers who have died will be raised and those alive will be transformed, and that all of them will meet the Lord and be with him for ever. They differ on timing, not on the fact.
Believers are not appointed to wrath
Every view teaches that God does not destine his people for his wrath, but for salvation through Christ. They differ on whether this means removal before trouble or protection within it.
Watch, because the day is unknown
All views call believers to readiness, holiness and faithful work. No one knows the day or the hour, and date-setting is rejected by careful teachers on every side.
The church suffers in this age

Every view agrees that Christians face tribulation and persecution now, and that God sustains them through it. Even those who expect escape from a future great tribulation affirm present suffering for Christ.
Christ reigns and will put every enemy down
All views confess that Jesus is now exalted at God's right hand and that his kingdom will triumph. Death will be destroyed, and God will make all things new.
